channel.title: Drugnews｜Taiwan Biotech Intelligence
channel.description: Independent biotech and pharmaceutical intelligence from Taiwan, covering clinical data, company strategy, licensing, valuation, and capital markets.

item.title: More Than $1 Billion in One Quarter: Why Did Alnylam Plunge 28%?
item.description: Amvuttra surpassed $1 billion in quarterly sales, yet Alnylam cut its TTR guidance and lost 28% in one day. The reset was not about RNAi technology failing; it was about pent-up demand normalizing, revenue concentration and the timing gap before a second commercial pillar arrives.

item.title: A $400 Billion Pharma Merger? AstraZeneca and Bristol Myers Squibb Are Reportedly Talking
item.description: AstraZeneca and BMS reportedly explored a combination with a combined market value approaching $400 billion. There is no announced transaction. The real questions are AstraZeneca's 2030 growth target, BMS's Eliquis and Opdivo exclusivity timeline, oncology-pipeline overlap, antitrust and whether integration can actually buy time.

item.title: Tau Earned a Retest: Why Biogen Is Taking Diranersen Into Phase 3 After CELIA Missed Its Primary Endpoint
item.description: CELIA missed its prespecified dose-response primary endpoint, yet the lowest dose produced a 0.54-point CDR-SB difference, or 26% slowing, while CSF total tau and tau PET moved in the expected direction. That is enough to justify Phase 3 planning, but not enough to declare tau a validated second disease-modifying pathway.

item.title: Bempikibart in Alopecia Areata: A 33-Patient Signal Is Not Yet a Win Over JAK Inhibitors
item.description: Q32 Bio nearly doubled after a 33-patient, single-arm Phase 2a readout. The investable questions are whether efficacy survives randomization, whether responses persist after treatment stops, and whether a larger safety database can support a differentiated place beside JAK inhibitors.

item.title: AnBogen Therapeutics: Building a “Starlink” for Cancer Immunotherapy
item.description: Can a small molecule from Taiwan extend the $30 billion PD-1 ecosystem into the 95% of metastatic colorectal cancer patients still beyond immunotherapy’s reach?

item.title: After Xtandi: Can Astellas Build an Oncology Platform?
item.description: Xtandi still dominates Astellas oncology sales. The real test is whether Padcev, Vyloy and the next CLDN18.2 assets can become a repeatable post-LOE platform.

item.title: Pelacarsen's HORIZON Test: Does Lowering Lp(a) Prevent Cardiovascular Events?
item.description: Pelacarsen can substantially lower Lp(a), but HORIZON must show whether biomarker reduction on top of standard care translates into fewer cardiovascular deaths, myocardial infarctions, strokes and urgent revascularizations.

item.title: T-cell Exhaustion Across PD-1, CAR-T and TCE: Immunotherapy's Next Contest Is Durability
item.description: PD-1 blockade, CAR-T and T-cell engagers ultimately depend on T cells that can expand, renew and persist. This analysis connects exhaustion biology, product engineering and clinical evidence to the next competitive threshold in immunotherapy.

item.title: $130 Billion in Six Months: Big Pharma Is Buying Time
item.description: Biopharma M&A accelerated in the first half of 2026, but BioSpace's 52 deals and IQVIA's 42 deals cannot be combined. The deeper story is that patent cliffs are pushing Big Pharma to pay for measurable clinical time.

item.title: Can a Pill Take Share from Injectables? The ICOTYDE Commercial Test
item.description: ICOTYDE generated more than 18,000 prescriptions in its first full quarter, showing demand for an oral IL-23R peptide. Valuation now depends on paid scripts, persistence, payer quality, and success beyond psoriasis.

item.title: Roche's Hidden Succession Engine: How 19 New Molecules Could Power the Next Growth Cycle
item.description: Roche generated CHF 47.669 billion in pharmaceutical sales in 2025, with Ocrevus, Hemlibra, and Vabysmo already accounting for roughly one-third of the total. The number that matters is not simply 19 potential new molecules, but whether giredestrant, fenebrutinib, obesity, Alzheimer's, and protein-degradation assets can inherit Roche's existing clinical, diagnostic, and commercial infrastructure on time.

item.title: SpaceX Goes to Orbit. Is the Money in the Crystals?
item.description: SpaceX is making low-Earth-orbit round trips more routine, but rockets do not discover drugs. From Keytruda crystallization and SpaceMD to Varda, UK regulation, and a Taiwan mission, this analysis asks whether microgravity-enabled manufacturing can pass the tests of repetition, scale-up, and regulation.

item.title: When a Biotech Says No to a Sale: Five Tests of Whether It Can Become a Biopharma
item.description: An acquisition is not the only successful outcome for a biotech. Using argenx, Insmed, Incyte, and Revolution Medicines as four operating snapshots, this analysis tests product evidence, cash generation, a second growth curve, global execution, and financing options—and shows what retaining control really costs.

item.title: Madrigal's MASH Platform Strategy: Rezdiffra as the Cornerstone, siRNA as the Next Growth Engine
item.description: Rezdiffra has opened the MASH market and built its commercialization infrastructure. Madrigal is now adding six Ribo siRNA programs and Arrowhead's ARO-PNPLA3 to create a cornerstone-plus-precision-combination treatment matrix.

item.title: Animal Studies Are Not Disappearing. Drug Development Rules Are Changing.
item.description: China's CDE PIONEER program opens a regulatory pathway for new approach methodologies. The real test is whether human-relevant evidence becomes reproducible, validated and reusable.

item.title: When ADCs Enter Autoimmune Disease: Precision Immune Modulation, Not More Killing
item.description: The opportunity for autoimmune ADCs is not to transplant oncology cytotoxins into immune cells. It is to deliver powerful glucocorticoids, small molecules, ASOs or siRNAs selectively to the cells that drive disease. LFD-200 offers an early human proof-of-mechanism signal for that thesis.

item.title: RevMed Upends Pancreatic Cancer Again: The RAS Combination Era Has Arrived
item.description: Daraxonrasib has already raised the bar with phase 3 overall-survival data. Early zoldonrasib combinations now suggest that pancreatic cancer's RAS competition is shifting from single agents to treatment ecosystems.

item.title: How to read FDA regulatory milestones: what each event changes—and what it does not
item.description: A practical guide to INDs, FDA designations, pivotal alignment, NDA/BLA review, PDUFA dates, advisory committees, complete response letters, and approval pathways.

item.title: How to read biotech licensing deals: from headline value to risk-adjusted economics
item.description: A practical guide to biotech licensing terms: upfront cash, milestones, royalties, territory, control, development obligations, supply, termination, and risk-adjusted deal economics.

item.title: How to read biotech clinical endpoints without overreading a positive headline
item.description: A practical guide to primary endpoints, effect size, confidence intervals, multiplicity, surrogate endpoints, and the questions that keep a positive biotech readout from being overread.

item.title: Big Pharma's New $10 Billion M&A Wave: Why Differentiation Now Beats Scale and Hype
item.description: Vertex's roughly $10 billion deal for Crinetics captures a wider change in Big Pharma's acquisition taste: away from scale and fashionable platforms, toward niche leadership, technological step-changes and commercial visibility.

item.title: After the Nobel Prize, Do Not Rush the First-Approved Treg Story: The Real Test Is Turning Immune Tolerance Into a Product
item.description: The Nobel Prize illuminated Treg biology, but commercial value will depend on whether immune tolerance can become a releasable, trackable, scalable and reimbursable product, not on an unverified first-approval headline.

item.title: The Next ADC War: Novartis Is Paying Up to $1.5 Billion for Myricx, but the Real Prize Is a New Payload Class
item.description: Novartis is paying up to $1.5 billion for Myricx. The strategic prize is not merely two ADC assets, but an NMT-inhibitor payload platform that could reopen the questions of therapeutic window, resistance and platform value.

item.title: Foundation Models Enter Drug Discovery: Anthropic Launches Claude Science as AI Companies Move Into the Real R&D Arena
item.description: Anthropic's launch of Claude Science and its move into drug discovery show foundation-model companies shifting from research tools into real R&D workflows. AI drug discovery will ultimately be judged by experiments, clinical data and tradable assets.

item.title: Winning First Is Not Winning: Roche's Divarasib Pushes KRAS Into a Generational Elimination Race
item.description: Roche's divarasib beat first-generation KRAS G12C inhibitors in a head-to-head Phase III study, moving the RAS field from proving druggability to replacing earlier products with harder clinical evidence.

item.title: Fasedienol's Phase 3 Brake: The Story Did Not Fail. The CNS Evidence Bar Did Its Job.
item.description: Fasedienol's PALISADE-4 miss was not simply a failed Phase 3 headline. It exposed the core CNS drug-development problem: a beautiful mechanism and a real unmet need still have to survive subjective endpoints, placebo response, patient selection, and a commercial repositioning test.

item.title: Sobi's NASP Received an FDA CRL: The Problem Was Manufacturing Credibility, Not Efficacy
item.description: FDA identified no clinical efficacy or safety concerns that affected NASP's approvability. The setback centered on CMC controls and contract-manufacturing deficiencies, showing biotech investors why manufacturing credibility becomes part of asset value near launch.

item.title: Why Has Japan Struggled to Build Global-Scale Biotech Companies?
item.description: Japan has strong science, major pharmaceutical companies, and a large drug market. The harder question is why that foundation has not produced more global-scale biotech startups. The answer is not scientific weakness, but an ecosystem gap across assets, talent, capital, clinical execution, and exits.

item.title: GLP-1's Second Half: Why Dorzagliatin Is About Making Metabolic Therapy Last
item.description: GLP-1 competition is moving from peak weight loss toward long-term use, tolerability, rebound control, and combination design. Dorzagliatin matters not as a GLP-1 replacement, but as a possible metabolic base for the next phase of chronic therapy.

item.title: Pfizer's ADC Bet: Why 3SBio's PD-1/VEGF Bispecific Has Become the New Pivot
item.description: After a Phase III setback for sigvotatug vedotin, Pfizer's $43 billion Seagen ADC bet is increasingly tied to whether 3SBio's PD-1/VEGF bispecific can become a new immuno-oncology combination backbone.

item.title: Off-the-Shelf CAR-T in 2026: Rebounding From the Trough
item.description: Off-the-shelf allogeneic CAR-T is no longer just a beautiful manufacturing story. In 2026, better clinical signals and clearer positioning are bringing the field back to the table.

item.title: Big Pharma's $134 Billion M&A Rush: What Is It Really Buying?
item.description: In the first half of 2026, Big Pharma's biotech M&A pace has accelerated sharply. The real question is not why large drugmakers have cash, but why they are suddenly less willing to wait.

item.title: Operation TrialBlazer: Why HHS Is Rewriting Clinical-Trial Rules and Biotech Competition
item.description: Operation TrialBlazer is not just an FDA efficiency program. It signals that the United States is treating clinical-trial speed as part of national biotech competitiveness, with direct implications for biotech valuation, financing windows, and regulatory strategy.

item.title: RevMed Says No to Being Bought: Biotech's Independent Era
item.description: Revolution Medicines is choosing not to make a sale its priority. The decision reflects a broader shift: top-tier biotech companies with breakthrough assets may once again have a credible path to grow into independent biopharma companies.

item.title: Synthetic Lethality After PARP: Why the Next Oncology Blockbuster Has Been So Hard to Find
item.description: PARP inhibitors turned synthetic lethality into a commercial reality. Two decades later, the industry is still asking why the next PARP-like blockbuster has been so difficult to reproduce.

item.title: Centanafadine’s Phase 3b Win: Why ADHD Treatment Is Moving Beyond Discipline and Toward Neurobiology
item.description: Otsuka’s centanafadine has reported positive Phase 3b data in adults with ADHD and comorbid anxiety. The FDA has accepted the NDA and granted priority review, making the program a useful lens for how ADHD treatment is shifting from behavioral stigma toward more precise neurobiological intervention.

item.title: GSK Goes Big: The $10.6B Nuvalent Deal Is Not Just a Lung-Cancer Pipeline Buy
item.description: GSK's $10.6 billion all-cash acquisition of Nuvalent is more than a late-stage lung-cancer pipeline deal. It is a strategic attempt to rebuild oncology, buy time before major revenue pressure, and regain a seat at the precision-oncology table.

item.title: The Largest Biotech IPO in US Market History: What Parabilis Is Really Teaching Investors
item.description: Parabilis Medicines' record-setting US biotech IPO is not a sign that speculative biotech is back. It shows that investors are willing to fund high-risk innovation when the platform, clinical asset, external validation, and capital-market window all line up.

item.title: The FDA Tone Has Shifted: Why Biotech’s Rebound Is Starting at the Regulatory Layer
item.description: Biotech’s recent rebound is not only a risk-on trade. FDA review signals, rare-disease flexibility, mRNA vaccine momentum, and renewed pharma M&A are changing how investors price clinical-stage assets.

item.title: Pancreatic Cancer Breakthrough: After RAS Inhibitors, PRMT5/MAT2A Combinations Open the Next Layer of Upside
item.description: Pancreatic cancer is moving into a new phase of precision combination therapy, as RAS inhibition meets MTAP-selective PRMT5 and MAT2A strategies.

item.title: Tirzepatide Enters Autoimmune Disease: Is Immunometabolism Lilly's Next Expansion Path?
item.description: Lilly is testing whether tirzepatide can move beyond weight loss and become part of an immunometabolism strategy for chronic immune-inflammatory diseases.

item.title: Toward the “Roche of Pet Medicine”: Protect Biotech’s Platform Bet
item.description: As companion animals age and owners become more willing to pay for serious-disease care, the next major question in pet medicine is whether a platform company can connect drugs, diagnostics, veterinary clinics, regulation, manufacturing, channels, and data into one defensible system.

item.title: Is the First AI-Designed Drug Finally Arriving? Takeda's Zasocitinib Beats Sotyktu Head-to-Head
item.description: Takeda's zasocitinib beat Sotyktu in a head-to-head Phase 3 psoriasis study, turning AI-enabled drug design into a real commercial test.

item.title: The Race for the Third Obesity-Drug Giant: Who Comes After Lilly and Novo Nordisk?
item.description: Lilly and Novo Nordisk dominate the first phase of the obesity-drug market. The next investment question is who can become the third major player by solving the problems GLP-1 leaders have not fully solved.

item.title: Merck's Shift on PD-1/VEGF Bispecifics: Keytruda Still Rules, but the Next IO Backbone Is Getting Closer
item.description: Merck's more serious positioning of MK-2010 suggests that PD-1/VEGF bispecifics are moving from a watch item to a strategic option in the post-Keytruda oncology landscape.

item.title: Enlivex's RAIN Token Windfall: When a Biotech Balance Sheet Starts Looking Like Crypto Treasury Strategy
item.description: Enlivex's paper gain from RAIN tokens shows how fragile biotech business models can create unusual treasury stories when operating revenue is absent and capital markets are difficult.

item.title: GSK's US$10.6 Billion Nuvalent Deal Is Really a Bet on Resistance and Brain Metastases
item.description: GSK is not merely buying three lung-cancer pipelines. It is buying a next-generation precision-oncology strategy around resistance, CNS activity, and cleaner kinase inhibition.

item.title: Ecnoglutide Versus Wegovy: A 20-Week Head-to-Head Signal Is Not the Same as a New GLP-1 King
item.description: Ecnoglutide's head-to-head weight-loss data versus semaglutide are interesting, but the GLP-1 race will be decided by long-term outcomes, tolerability, labels, supply, and global evidence.

item.title: Why Would Lilly, the Obesity-Drug Giant, Spend US$3.8 Billion on Vaccine Companies?
item.description: Lilly's vaccine acquisitions show that the company is using obesity-drug cash flow to widen its long-term disease-prevention and immunology strategy.

item.title: ASCO 2026: RAS, ADCs, Bispecifics, and In Vivo CAR-T Point to a New Oncology Cycle
item.description: ASCO 2026 showed that oncology is moving from single-mechanism breakthroughs toward platform combinations across RAS targeting, ADCs, PD-1/VEGF bispecifics, and in vivo CAR-T.

item.title: Revolution Medicines: Why Biotech Winners Need Capital Strategy, Not Just Good Science
item.description: Revolution Medicines shows why next-generation biotech companies need to convert clinical momentum into capital momentum if they want to finish expensive global drug-development races.

item.title: The Next Phase of AI Drug Development: Making Molecules Survive as Drugs
item.description: AI drug development is moving from molecular generation to clinical survival. AnHorn Medicines shows how AI+PROTAC, experimental feedback, and human translation may form a Taiwan-born clinical-asset engine.

item.title: Where Does AI Drug Discovery Stand Now? A Pipeline-Based Reality Check
item.description: AI drug discovery has moved beyond the concept stage and into clinical validation. This article reviews Zasocitinib, GB-0895, Zovegalisib, and REC-4881 to examine how different AI strategies are being converted into real drug assets.

item.title: Obesity Becomes King: How GLP-1 Is Reshuffling Global Biotech Capital
item.description: GLP-1 is no longer only a weight-loss topic. It is redirecting biotech capital, BD urgency, manufacturing attention, and valuation imagination across global pharma.

item.title: RAS Targeting Opens a New Pancreatic-Cancer Window: How Senhwa's CX-5461 Positions for the Next Resistance-Management War
item.description: Daraxonrasib opens a new pancreatic-cancer window, but the next value question is resistance management. Senhwa's CX-5461 matters if it can become a rational combination partner.

item.title: Biotech IR Is Not Making Slides Prettier; It Is Turning Pipelines Into Trackable Capital-Market Stories
item.description: Biotech IR is not cosmetic storytelling. Good IR turns clinical, CMC, regulatory, commercial, and financing milestones into a capital-market narrative that investors can actually track.

item.description: Curium's rumored interest in Lantheus is best read as a bid for nuclear-medicine infrastructure: isotope access, hospital channels, imaging workflow, and radiopharma commercialization depth.

item.title: CAR-T Enters a New Era: From Blood Cancer to Autoimmune Disease
item.description: CAR-T's move from blood cancer into autoimmune disease could redefine cell therapy, but the value depends on whether deep immune reset can justify manufacturing complexity, safety risk, and cost.

item.title: Drugmakers Without AI Capability May No Longer Be Called Drugmakers
item.description: AI is becoming a core operating capability for pharma, but its value comes from improving discovery, translation, trial design, and portfolio decisions rather than from marketing language alone.

item.title: Old Targets Are Crowded, but They Can Still Make Money
item.description: Crowded drug targets can still create value when companies differentiate through patient selection, formulation, route of administration, clinical design, pricing, or commercial channel strategy.

item.title: Starting With Ruxolitinib Cream: Why Not Every JAK Molecule Can Become a Topical Drug
item.description: Topical JAK drugs are not won by target biology alone. The real value lies in skin delivery, local exposure, systemic safety, indication choice, and whether the product can fit daily dermatology practice.

item.title: Retatrutide Moves Toward Surgery-Level Weight Loss: Lilly's Triple-Agonist Pushes Obesity Treatment Into a New Arena
item.description: Retatrutide pushes obesity-drug efficacy toward surgery-level territory, but the real competitive battle will be durability, tolerability, body composition, comorbidity benefit, and access.
